habitat: Usually solitary at floodplains, pans and rivers in well-wooded country. Large influxes occur in summer in northern Botswana and the Zambezi Valley.
summary: A sparse resident and a common summer visitor. The neck and head are woolly white, the face is black, and the body is chocolate-brown and looks black. The bill and legs are dark red. The undertail coverts project beyond the tail. The immature is duller, with a horn-coloured bill. Newman’s page uses the name Ciconia episcopus.

similar.note: Black Stork has a red bill and a white belly, and no woolly white neck.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^4=16 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 8–32.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

White head, black face and dark red bill.
Dark body. The undertail coverts project beyond the tail.

calls.description: No call was described, and no usable recording was found.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Newman also calls it a common summer visitor. No recording was stored under Ciconia microscelis, and the Asian woolly-necked recordings were not used for this split. The call text is a gap. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.
